shopify_order_signal.interpretation: The native flow moved sample purchases from draft-order creation to normal web checkout. This can change which sample purchases fire or qualify for the Google Shopping App Purchase conversion even though the sample products are not advertised.

google_ads_pre_post.interpretation: The 28-day window is consistent with conversion-mix dilution, not worse traffic: attributed conversion count rose while average attributed conversion value fell, CPC fell, and CTR improved. Aggregate data cannot prove which Google-attributed conversions were sample orders.

budget_changes.window: 14 days before versus 14 days after, excluding change day
budget_changes.interpretation: The cut reduced volume nearly in proportion to spend, while CPC was nearly flat. The ROAS comparison is confounded by unusually large pre-change orders and the April pricing incident.

The increase expanded traffic without raising CPC materially. The ROAS sign reverses between the 7-day and 14-day windows, so these data do not show a stable causal efficiency loss from the budget increase.

google_ads.interpretation: July is worse through July 19. Against matched June days, nearly unchanged spend produced 31% less attributed value. Higher traffic cost and lower average conversion value are the main measurable drivers; conversion rate was only modestly lower.

shopify_all_channel_context.interpretation: All-channel Shopify order activity improved in July while Google-attributed Max-2 value declined. Native samples remained about 72% of valid orders in both matched windows, so sample share did not increase materially, though absolute native sample volume rose 37%.

google_ads_rolling_19_day_windows.baseline_dates: Window starts 2026-01-01 through 2026-06-12 and ends by 2026-06-30
google_ads_rolling_19_day_windows.caveat: Rolling windows overlap heavily, so the percentile and frequency are descriptive rather than independent statistical tests.

random_variation_test.interpretation: The size of the July decline is consistent with ordinary large-order timing: one historical 95th-percentile attributed order would almost erase the matched-period ROAS gap. The absolute July ROAS level is nevertheless unusually low and should be monitored over a 56-90 day window. All-channel Shopify revenue and large-order counts improved in July, so there is no corresponding store-wide demand collapse.

limitations: Shopify orders and Google Ads conversions are compared in aggregate; they are not joined at the order or click level.
A native sample order can affect Google Smart Bidding only when it is attributed to Google Ads and included in the campaign's primary purchase goal.
The May 16 budget increase, May 28 Merchant Center catalog change, and May 30 native sample rollout are close together and confound simple pre/post comparisons.
Sample purchases carry downstream value that is only partly captured inside Google's 30-day attribution window.
